subproblem.title: Blow-up of a flat slab: flatness of spt T at scale σ rescales to flatness of the blow-up at scale 1
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), every x ∈ ℝ^P, all reals σ > 0 and β, and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P (Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), with p_Q = Q.starProjection the orthogonal projection onto Q: if |(y − x) − p_Q(y − x)| < β·σ for every y ∈ spt T with |y − x| < σ (dist y x < σ), then every u ∈ spt(η_{x,σ#}T) = spt(blowUp T x σ) with |u| < 1 satisfies |u − p_Q(u)| < β.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (σ β : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ y ∈ T.support, dist y x < σ → ‖(y - x) - Q.starProjection (y - x)‖ < β * σ) → ∀ u ∈ (blowUp T x σ hσ.ne').support, ‖u‖ < 1 → ‖u - Q.starProjection u‖ < β
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (supports of the blow-ups). Notation: η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x), in Lean dilation x σ y = −(σ⁻¹ • x) + σ⁻¹ • y; p_Q = Q.starProjection is a (continuous) linear map.
1. By dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) (accepted: for σ > 0, spt(blowUp T x σ) = dilation x σ '' spt T), the hypothesis u ∈ spt(blowUp T x σ) provides y ∈ spt T with u = η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x).
2. Multiplying by σ ≠ 0 gives y − x = σu. Hence dist(y, x) = |y − x| = σ|u| < σ·1 = σ, using σ > 0 and |u| < 1.
3. By the hypothesis applied to y ∈ spt T with dist(y, x) < σ: |(y − x) − p_Q(y − x)| < βσ. By linearity of p_Q, (y − x) − p_Q(y − x) = σu − p_Q(σu) = σ(u − p_Q(u)), whose norm is σ|u − p_Q(u)| because σ > 0. So σ|u − p_Q(u)| < βσ, and dividing by σ > 0 gives |u − p_Q(u)| < β. ∎
proof_key_steps: dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) writes u = η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x) with y ∈ spt T.
Then y − x = σu and |y − x| = σ|u| < σ, so the flatness hypothesis applies to y.
By linearity (y − x) − p_Q(y − x) = σ(u − p_Q u), so σ|u − p_Q u| < βσ and |u − p_Q u| < β.

audit.reason: The accepted support transformation supplies y with y − x = σu. The norm bound permits application of flatness, and linearity of starProjection followed by division by positive σ proves the conclusion. The argument correctly allows arbitrary β and arbitrary U, as stated.
